conventions.convention: Time is rescaled to [0,1]; the unknown period θ is positive and constant. The augmented field is (θf(x),0), and the boundary residual is (x1−x0,ψ(x0)).
The affine phase is transverse precisely when cᵀf(x*)≠0; positive period alone does not exclude stationary solutions.
Validated Euler uses the coordinate maximum norm, exact rational set arithmetic, and sound magnitude and Lipschitz bounds on the entire compact convex tube.
Midpoint interior residuals are divided by h; nodal and residual norms are maxima of Euclidean block norms.
The parameterized shooting jet orders variables as (x,μ,θ); section-mode consumers ordered as (x,θ,μ) must permute Jacobian columns.
Cluster contours are simple counterclockwise strictly convex polygons; counts use algebraic multiplicity and the complex infinity matrix norm.
A validated root requires a complete Krawczyk partition with exactly one unique-root box, all other boxes root-free, a separate contraction bound, and a field component excluding zero.

load_bearing.statement: On a successful run with the specified sound oracle and tube bounds, every admitted augmented IVP exists through time 1, lies in the returned cell tubes, and ends in Y_N; the endpoint and matrix blocks enclose φ_θ(x0) and D_xφ_θ(x0).

At the stated nonstationary phase-fixed periodic point, J=[[M−I,f*],[cᵀ,0]] is invertible if and only if 1 is an algebraically simple eigenvalue of M and cᵀf*≠0; the Statement also supplies its explicit Euclidean inverse-norm bound.

A validated shooting jet encloses the endpoint, residual, every shooting Jacobian, trajectory, and physical monodromy over the input box; admissible success requires the specified successful augmented Euler runs and period-column range query.
A certified-count(c) return implies that every matrix in the nonempty supplied family has exactly c eigenvalues in the polygon interior, counted with algebraic multiplicity, and none on its boundary.

Under the stated successful corrector record, there is exactly one shooting zero in Z, it lies in Y, generates a phase-fixed nonconstant positive-period solution, and its exact trajectory and monodromy lie in the returned enclosures.

For a least-period nonconstant orbit with algebraically simple phase multiplier and the stated transverse phase section, the Poincare derivative eigenvalues are exactly the monodromy multipliers other than the single phase multiplier, with algebraic multiplicity.

For the stated augmented periodic solution with simple neutral multiplier and transverse phase, the continuous linearized BVP operator is bijective and its inverse norm is bounded by the explicit K_L in the Statement.

concerns.concern: The Inputs admit a 'rational candidate box' Z, and Independent validation says to 'run [[alg-krawczyk-root-certification]] on F and Z'. That supplier requires an initial real box under def-real-boxes-and-interval-jacobian-enclosures, whose endpoints must be finite dyadics. An admitted rational endpoint such as 1/3 is not dyadic, and no conversion or generalized rational-box interface is specified. Thus the supplier call is outside its stated input domain for some allowed inputs. The same rational-versus-dyadic convention should be checked in def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure, which accepts rational Q while saying its boxes use that real-box definition.

seams_checked.note: Correction equations and finite-budget Newton calls preserve singularity, domain, and budget branches; tolerance attainment is not promoted to exact-root certification.

The augmented BVP remains square. Numerical endpoint derivatives are distinguished from exact-flow sensitivities; normalized midpoint rows and block norms agree. The mesh-uniform inverse is used conditionally, with K supplied explicitly.
The adapter retains the previous section normal, current tangent predictor, chart and angle checks, finite budgets, conditional callback termination, and separate fold checks.
Floquet and Poincare conventions agree. The stability proof reduces a possibly repeated certified period to the least period and establishes phase transversality before invoking return-map stability.
The complex infinity norm and resolvent-cover bounds are preserved. The cover is used only for boundary invertibility and a resolvent bound; eigenvalue counting is proved separately.

Existence, separate contraction-based uniqueness, inverse witness, and unresolved-box restrictions are preserved. However, the periodic corrector passes an arbitrary rational box to a supplier whose real-box contract requires dyadic endpoints; see the concern on alg-validated-periodic-orbit-corrector.
